headline: Graph models couple network topology with pairwise and multi-view relations in biology
label: Graph Learning For Biological Networks
summary: Recent work applies graph neural and hypergraph models to gene regulatory, drug response, and host-virus interaction prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit modeling of relational topology in biological networks rather than flat feature tables. In gene regulatory work, scGPL pairs global regulatory graph structure with pairwise TF-target interactions on scRNA-seq data, and scAdaG2M applies graph-to-MLP distillation to scRNA-seq clustering to address over-smoothing. Drug-centred items use multi-view designs: GLH2Syn combines global diffusion with structure-aware local learning on a heterogeneous hypergraph, MTDKF fuses metapath topology with domain knowledge for miRNA-drug-disease triplets, and MulDR preserves omics-specific cell-line relations. HV-MultiScaleGNN compares local, global, and combined graph views for host-virus protein interactions. The distinctive element is the separation and recombination of local and global relational views, or of topology and auxiliary knowledge, rather than a single pooled graph.
